text: True or False: The no-false-lemmas condition (Harman), added to JTB, successfully handles the fake-barn (barn-facade) case, because that case turns on a false intermediate belief in the subject's reasoning.
explanation: False. In the fake-barn case the subject forms the belief 'there is a barn' directly from perceiving a genuine barn, with no false lemma anywhere in the reasoning, yet intuitively lacks knowledge because of the surrounding facades. The case therefore shows that no-false-lemmas is not sufficient to rule out all Gettier-style failures: here the luck is environmental rather than inferential.
